metadata.sampling_design: Stratified scenario allocation with a declared latent-factor Gaussian copula, shared shocks across alternatives, marginal-preserving inverse transforms, and matched independent/correlation-stress counterfactuals.

decision.title: Inclusive Urban Regeneration Strategy
decision.domain: Urban planning, place-based policy, systems analysis, and public finance
decision.question: Choose a five-year regeneration strategy that improves access and economic opportunity without exceeding fiscal or displacement-risk tolerances.
blocking_reasons: evidence is not labeled for operational use
decision.feasibility_basis: one-sided 95% upper confidence bound on simulated constraint-breach frequency

status-quo.label: Status quo grants
status-quo.description: Continue small competitive grants without a coordinated land or transit strategy.

transit-corridor.label: Transit-led mixed-income corridor
transit-corridor.description: Coordinate bus rapid transit, inclusionary housing, and station-area development.

innovation-district.label: Innovation district
innovation-district.description: Use anchor-institution investment, commercial zoning, and research-space incentives.

neighborhood-retrofit.label: Neighborhood retrofit and anti-displacement
neighborhood-retrofit.description: Fund building retrofits, community land ownership, small-business support, and targeted accessibility upgrades.

factors.label: Systemic adverse demand and delivery shock
factors.description: A shared latent shock moves outcome distributions across criteria and alternatives in the adverse direction; signs follow each criterion's value direction.

evidence.type: Synthetic spatial-policy appraisal and scenario assumptions
evidence.as_of: Synthetic demonstration; no production as-of date
sources: Illustrative parcel and transit accessibility summaries
evidence.causal_claim_status: No causal claim; economic and displacement effects are modeled planning assumptions.
limitations: Spatial spillovers across neighboring districts are simplified.
Distributional outcomes are represented with three community groups.
Delivery timelines do not include litigation or permitting appeals.
The Gaussian copula and factor loadings are synthetic assumptions; tail dependence may differ in real data and requires domain approval.

decision_notes: A real plan should use parcel-level and travel-time analysis and publish neighborhood distributional results.
Community preferences should influence weights through a documented deliberative process.
